status: partial implementation for the active 36-feature goal
behavior: Typed requests must explicitly reference a current selection, page, file, window or application; negated actions and mismatched native/browser reference types fail closed.
Sage checks for reviewed families before requesting any foreground observation; page text is requested only for explicit page references.

A deterministic local lexical scorer compares the bounded reference against reviewed branch aliases and next steps; it returns one path or at most two close alternatives and never exposes reference text.
The preview is advisory. Selecting a button fills the composer only; submission and all normal scope, policy, approval and verification gates remain unchanged.
No model, AI API, downloaded weights, provider, service or dependency is used for prediction; reference text is transient and is not persisted or sent to a planner.
The regular grammar preview is emitted first. Context capture and scoring are best-effort on the asynchronous preview path with a two-second deadline.

validation.workspace_tests: cargo test --workspace --locked passed: sage-core 196 passed and 7 ignored; sage-browser-worker 1 passed; remaining binary, protocol and doc-test targets passed.
validation.format_and_diff: cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed.
validation.windows: MainWindow.xaml and App.xaml parsed as XML. dotnet is unavailable, so Windows C# compilation and live interaction were not run.
validation.latency: Release scorer benchmark on Apple M3, 1,000 runs over 120 synthetic family objects (the pairwise upper bound from the 16-routine cap) and a 7.5 KiB page: p50 350,959 ns, p95 424,458 ns, p99 641,958 ns. Scoring only; excludes SQLite loading, native/browser capture, IPC, rendering and user-perceived latency.

limitations: Feature 35 remains partial: branch scores are heuristic and have no calibrated confidence; broader context sources, context-conditioned synthesis and explicitly authorized automatic prefixes remain open.
